Here's a few things I would like as a general rules:

  • I'd like Screenshot Saturday to require you to comment on someone else's post to post your own. This is to stop our threads from becoming as bad as /r/gamedev's.

  • I want any blog posts or other text media to be at least summarized (or copied completely) in a self post. This would be to prevent dead links and overloaded servers.

  • Some kind of weekly thread specific to us? Flashback Friday, Tutor Tuesday, just ad-libbing here. Please do suggest things.

  • Cross posts would be good, since Voat is semi-starved for content, especially for smaller communities (e.g not /v/funny).

In Myanmar, Garment Factories That Source Popular Brand-Name Clothing Retailers Aim To Defeat A 40-Cent Hourly Minimum Wage

So what? Yes, from our point of view working in a factory for less than 40 cents per hour sounds awful. But for the people in these countries it's most likely the best opportunity they have. If they had better work opportunities, there would be no need for them to do this kind of work.

Pretty much all countries started their path to industrialization like that, even in Europe and America. To have a modern and more productive society you have to start somewhere to increase the skills and capital for automation and thus a higher productivity. Many of the emerging Asian countries produced cheap clothing a few decades ago. Now they can produce electronics or other stuff of higher value and the cheap clothing production moves to the next country, in this case Myanmar.

If you try to enforce the laws and values of an already industrialized country on one just starting, you're most likely causing more harm than good. You can't just change the law and do stuff like impose a higher minimum wage, prohibit child labor, and expect the country to magically become full of skilled people with capital for machinery over night to sustain that. Even if it's hard to accept for many, because "someone ought to do something!", these countries have to go through the sweat shop phase to reduce their reliance on manual agriculture. A good example is Bangladesh. Some western organizations lobbied for stricter child labor laws, because children should go to school instead of working a factory. But this seemingly good intended law had the "unexpected" consequences that the families didn't earn enough money anymore, so the kids were sent to illegal and even worse jobs, like prostitution, so they don't have to starve. No parents send their kids to a factory instead of a school if they don't have to. And remember, the long summer break in school that still exists in America and Europe has it's origin in the need for the kids to work in the fields during harvest. Because until just about a century ago, every country on this planet had child labor.
